metadata.title: CrowdStrike explores acquisition of Zscaler – report

content.text:
US cybersecurity provider CrowdStrike is considering the acquisition of cloud security provider Zscaler in a deal that could rank among the cybersecurity sector's "largest" transactions, Bloomberg reported.
The talks are continuing, and sources cited by the news outlet said there is no certainty that they will result in an agreement.
Verdict has approached CrowdStrike and Zscaler for comment.
Zscaler, which is based in California, had a market valuation of $32bn at the close of regular trading on Friday, 20 November 2026.
CrowdStrike has a market capitalisation of around $235bn, according to the report.
Zscaler reported record revenue of $3.35bn for fiscal 2026. The company has not reported an annual profit since it listed publicly in 2018, while its shares had fallen by more than 13% this year before the takeover report emerged.
The company provides cloud-native technology intended to replace legacy virtual private network (VPN) appliances supplied by companies including Citrix and Ivanti.
Zscaler is said to cater to about 11,000 corporate customers worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 500, in over 185 countries.
A transaction would bring together CrowdStrike's Falcon endpoint and server security platform with Zscaler's secure access service edge and zero-trust network technology.
The combined environments would broaden visibility across devices, cloud applications, and corporate networks as businesses respond to AI-driven threats.
The reported discussions come during a period of cybersecurity-sector consolidation.
Alphabet agreed last year to acquire cybersecurity start-up Wiz for $32bn, while ServiceNow reached a $7.75bn agreement to buy Armis in December.
Palo Alto Networks acquired CyberArk for $25bn in February, followed by an all-stock transaction for Applied Compute valued at $4.5bn this month.
Earlier this month, CrowdStrike also signed a definitive agreement to acquire Silicon Valley startup Fiddler AI, an AI agent observability and explainability company.
US infrastructure outages affecting Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase & Co, United Airlines, and the National Security Agency this month have also shaped the industry backdrop.
"CrowdStrike explores acquisition of Zscaler – report" was originally created and published by Verdict, a GlobalData owned brand.
